newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks battered as blue-chip boom peters out.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks battered as blue-chip boom peters out.

text.p: Tokyo stocks tumbled Monday as a recent boom in blue chips faded, triggering a wave of selling that pushed the key market index below the 21,000 level.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average shed 1.64 percent of its value in a steep and swift slide at the end of an otherwise dull session, falling 345.67 points to finish at 20,674.69.
Brokers said the fading interest in big-name global shares pulled away one of the main props for the market and the fall was accentuated by thin volume.

"The Nikkei average is likely to gauge the bottom of the recent range this week, after it tested the upper side last week," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd. "The focus is on whether it will be supported at around 20,500," he said.

The recent rally in blue-chip issues had been led by foreign investors, whose aggressive buying helped buoy the overall market. The buying was fuelled by solid half-year profits announced by the blue-chip companies during the earnings season in November, brokers said.
But the euphoria has since ebbed and no other buying factors have appeared to keep up the momentum, brokers said.
Turnover was a thin 224 million shares on Monday, down from Friday's 292 million shares.
Declining issues beat advancing ones 856 to 225, while 171 issues were unchanged.
The broader TOPIX index also fell, dropping 20.61 points or 1.32 percent to end at 1,542.19, while the Nikkei 300 average was 4.31 points or 1.46 percent lower at 291.25.

The market has been recently split into winning sectors such as automobiles and electronics, including corporate high fliers like Toyota and NEC Corp., which had continued to set record highs, and weak sectors which have languished at their year's lows, brokers said.
"In that situation, new sectors have not appeared to support the buying trend," Ishijima said.
Brokers said loss-cutting sales by dealers accelerated after the Nikkei average fell below 21,000.
Trading was mostly subdued until shortly before the close, when the sell-off took hold, they said.
